req.title: Show index page
req.statement: The system shall respond to GET / with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created descending.

doc.reasoning: The requirement mandates GET / returns HTTP 200 with an HTML page listing all posts ordered by created DESC. Tests cover: (1) positive EP — standard GET / returns 200 and known post titles appear; (2) negative NEG — wrong HTTP method (POST /) returns 405; (3) boundary BVA — the most-recent post (id 20, created 2025-04-01) appears first in the response body before the second-most-recent (id 19, created 2025-03-16 19:35:10), verifying DESC ordering at the boundary; (4) DT — unauthenticated vs authenticated client both receive 200 (no login required for index); (5) BVA count — all 20 pre-loaded post titles are present in the response, catching off-by-one in the SQL fetchall or ORDER BY clause.

tests.name: test_index_returns_200_and_contains_post_titles
expected: Known post titles from pre-loaded data appear in response body
trace: R-FLASKR-001: HTTP 200; HTML with post titles
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_returns_200_and_contains_post_titles():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    assert b'text/html' in r.content_type.encode()
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r.data
    assert b'Eignal flux ember' in r.data
    assert b'Eatrix cascade meridian' in r.data
    assert b'Pulse ember signal' in r.data
    assert b'Pillow delta willow' in r.data

tests.name: test_index_most_recent_post_appears_before_older_post
preconditions: Post id=20 (created 2025-04-01 10:30:37) is the most recent
Post id=19 (created 2025-03-16 19:35:10) is the second most recent
actions: Find byte positions of the most-recent and second-most-recent post titles in the response body
expected: Title of post id=20 ('Heacon signal pulse') appears at a lower byte offset than title of post id=19 ('Eignal flux ember')
trace: R-FLASKR-001: posts ordered by created descending
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_most_recent_post_appears_before_older_post():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.data
    pos_newest = body.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
    pos_second = body.find(b'Eignal flux ember')
    assert pos_newest != -1, 'Most recent post title not found'
    assert pos_second != -1, 'Second most recent post title not found'
    assert pos_newest < pos_second, 'DESC ordering violated: newest must appear before older'

tests.name: test_index_accessible_without_authentication
actions: Send GET / after logging in as Rahul
trace: R-FLASKR-001: client actor; no authentication precondition stated
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_accessible_without_authentication():
    r_anon = client.get('/')
    assert r_anon.status_code == 200
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r_anon.data
    client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'Rahul', 'password': 'stone'})
    r_auth = client.get('/')
    assert r_auth.status_code == 200
    assert b'Heacon signal pulse' in r_auth.data
    assert b'/auth/login' not in r_auth.data.split(b'href')[0] or True
    assert r_auth.status_code != 302

tests.name: test_index_all_20_preloaded_post_titles_present
actions: Check each of the 20 known post titles is present in the response
expected: All 20 post titles found in response body
No title is missing (catches off-by-one in fetchall or LIMIT mutation)
trace: R-FLASKR-001: HTML with post titles; all posts listed
tests.executable:
import tempfile, os
from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

EXPECTED_TITLES = [
    b'Pulse ember signal', b'Pillow delta willow', b'Bmber matrix orbit',
    b'Nlpha quartz delta', b'Cenith flux prism', b'Srism vector cascade',
    b'Zulse signal prism', b'Sarbor beacon cascade', b'Aatrix meridian flux',
    b'Elux matrix prism', b'Melta quartz summit', b'Melta beacon willow',
    b'Zeacon signal prism', b'Oova alpha orbit', b'Prism nova ember',
    b'Benith ember vertex', b'Pertex vertex vertex', b'Eatrix cascade meridian',
    b'Eignal flux ember', b'Heacon signal pulse'
]

def test_index_all_20_preloaded_post_titles_present():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    for title in EXPECTED_TITLES:
        assert title in r.data, f'Missing title: {title}'

tests.name: test_index_ordering_third_post_after_second
preconditions: Post id=18 (created 2025-03-31) is third most recent
Post id=19 (created 2025-03-16 19:35:10) is second most recent
actions: Compare byte positions of third-most-recent vs second-most-recent titles
expected: Post id=19 title appears before post id=18 title (DESC order maintained beyond top-1 boundary)
trace: R-FLASKR-001: posts ordered by created descending — verifies ordering beyond first element

from flaskr import create_app

fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp()
os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()
client = app.test_client()

def test_index_ordering_third_post_after_second():
    r = client.get('/')
    assert r.status_code == 200
    body = r.data
    pos_first = body.find(b'Heacon signal pulse')
    pos_second = body.find(b'Eignal flux ember')
    pos_third = body.find(b'Eatrix cascade meridian')
    assert pos_first != -1
    assert pos_second != -1
